catches: $50 goes to both sides: the referrer receives $50 and the referred friend receives $50 when the friend opens a new personal QCBT checking account.

Friend requirements are strict: new consumer client only, Visa debit card used at least once (point-of-sale only; ATM transactions do not qualify), requirements met within 6 months of opening, account open at least 30 calendar days with a positive balance at payout.

Bonuses are reported to the IRS as applicable; recipients are responsible for applicable taxes.

steps: Existing Quad City Bank & Trust client fills in name, phone, and QCBT account view on the Refer-A-Friend card.
Client gives the card to a friend (new QCBT consumer checking client, Iowa/Illinois resident).
Friend opens a new personal QCBT checking account and uses the new QCBT Visa debit card at least once within 6 months of opening (point-of-sale; ATM transactions do not qualify).

Once the qualifying activity is met and the account has been open at least 30 calendar days with a positive balance, both parties receive their $50 bonus as an account credit within 30 calendar days, provided neither account is closed.
timing: Bonus paid as an account credit within 30 calendar days of the qualifying activity being met, provided both the current client and referred account are not closed, the account has been open at least 30 calendar days, and has a positive balance at payout.
when_cash_arrives: Bonus paid as an account credit within 30 calendar days of the qualifying activity being met, provided both the current client and referred account are not closed, the account has been open at least 30 calendar days, and has a positive balance at payout. Paid after your friend completes the program's activity requirements - the friend's qualification is the gating step.
maximize: Have your friend knock out transaction counts in a single day (small purchases) and set up direct deposit on the first paycheck - do not let activity dribble across the window.
Verify the exact qualification checklist with the institution before referring - thin-terms programs often have unpublished requirements that void referrals.
Structural reason it cannot be faster: you only get paid if the friend completes real banking activity; a join-and-idle referral earns nothing.
